title: Week 4: Two Unbeaten Kings, Two Winless Jesters
synopsis: Week 4 crowns Prestige Worldwide as the undisputed number one after a monstrous 301-point demolition, while The Many-Faced Squad survives by the skin of their teeth and two squads remain winless at the bottom of the barrel.
script:
Good evening fantasy fanatics and welcome back to THE NUTCAST -- your weekly audio deep-dive into the only dynasty league that matters: The NUT Fantasy Football League! I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, and folks, Week 4 just sorted the wheat from the chaff, the champs from the chumps, the winners from the… well, you'll see. Let's crack some shells!

First things first: we have a new sheriff in town. Prestige Worldwide didn't just win this week -- they laid down the law with a biblical beating. Cincy_kid's squad dropped THREE HUNDRED AND ONE POINT SEVEN FIVE on poor Gus Swayze's Squad. That's not a typo, people -- 301.75! That's a margin of victory of one hundred fifteen point six. Let me say that again: ONE HUNDRED FIFTEEN POINT SIX. Gus Swayze's Squad put up a respectable 186 points, which would've won three other matchups this week, and they still got blown out like a birthday candle in a wind tunnel. Tetairoa McMillan went absolutely nuclear with 38.2 points, Kenneth Walker added 30.4, and the whole roster was firing on all cylinders. Prestige Worldwide is now 4-and-0, sitting pretty at the top of the Power Rankings with an 87.9 composite score, and they've officially taken the throne. The league bank is loving those FAAB taxes too -- Prestige cashed in on a ten-dollar bet against the 29.5-point spread and collected another ten bucks for the vault.

But if you want drama, if you want nail-biters, if you want the kind of game that makes you refresh your app every thirty seconds -- then you were watching The Many-Faced Squad versus Boom Goes The Dynamite. CamWells16's Many-Faced Squad came in as a 6.5-point favorite, and they won by exactly 2.8 points. That's it. That's the margin. 175.95 to 173.14. Bijan Robinson put up 27.2 for The Many-Faced Squad, but Nico Collins fired back with 27.3 for Boom Goes The Dynamite and Ernest Jones added 27 more. It came down to the wire and The Many-Faced Squad stayed undefeated at 4-and-0, but man, they felt every single one of those points. That's your closest game of the week, and it was the kind of sweat that makes dynasty ball worth playing.

Now let's talk about the flip side. The OG Champ limped into Week 4 at 1-and-2, faced Lickety Splitz Squad as a 29.5-point underdog, and put up the week's lowest score: 158.78. Twillie391's Lickety Splitz Squad handled business with 199.25, led by T.J. Watt's 25.5 and Puka Nacua's 23.2. The OG Champ got a nice 28.5 from Byron Young on defense, but Zack Baun laid a goose egg and Dalton Kincaid managed just 1.2. JeffPeterson20 falls to 1-and-3 and drops to ninth in the standings. Meanwhile, Lickety Splitz Squad cashed not one but TWO ten-dollar FAAB bets on that 29.5-point spread -- that's twenty bucks flowing into the league bank, folks, and the house always wins.

White Center Rats kept rolling, improving to 3-and-1 with a 209.32 to 173.64 victory over Breece & Desist. CeeDee Lamb went off for 32.8 points and Jared Goff added a clean 20.48. Savro24's squad also collected ten dollars on a FAAB bet -- twice! -- so that's another twenty into the vault. The Rats are sitting third in the Power Rankings and looking dangerous.

JSN Your Face came into the week with a chance to even up at 2-and-2, and they did exactly that, rolling past Points Against Champion 212.22 to 164.19. Javonte Williams balled out with 28.8, Drake Maye added 27.16, and BillsMafia1480 covered the 16.5-point spread with room to spare. JSN Your Face climbs to sixth in the standings and eighth in the Power Rankings.

And then there are the two squads staring up from the bottom of the barrel. Love Hurts drops to 0-and-4 after losing 187.42 to 166.61 to Price is wrong BItch!, and Gus Swayze's Squad is also 0-and-4 after that aforementioned demolition. KShrewsberry and AlanCarignan are both officially in Toilet Bowl territory, and the season is getting away fast. Love Hurts actually had Chuba Hubbard drop 25.4, but it wasn't nearly enough. Price is wrong BItch! moves to 2-and-2 and jumps two spots in the standings to eighth.

Let's hit the individual performances. Your league-wide top scorer this week was Tetairoa McMillan with that monster 38.2. Kyren Williams added 33.2 for Gus Swayze despite the loss, CeeDee Lamb torched for 32.8, Kenneth Walker put up 30.4, Javonte Williams had 28.8, and Byron Young logged 28.5 on the defensive side. Those are the players who put teams on their backs.

On the flip side, we had four players lay absolute goose eggs: Rashee Rice and Mason Graham both put up zeroes for JSN Your Face, Zack Baun gave The OG Champ nothing, and Derwin James blanked for Price is wrong BItch!. Saquon Barkley managed just 1.5 for Boom Goes The Dynamite -- that's the kind of performance that costs you close games.

Looking at the Power Rankings, Prestige Worldwide claims the crown at number one, Lickety Splitz Squad jumps up to two, and White Center Rats holds steady at three. The biggest mover? Boom Goes The Dynamite slides from fourth to fifth after that razor-thin loss, while The Many-Faced Squad drops from five to six despite staying undefeated. Funny how that works -- win your games but don't look pretty doing it, and the composite score doesn't care about your record.

So as we close the book on Week 4, we've got two teams sitting pretty at 4-and-0, two teams drowning at 0-and-4, and everyone else fighting for position in the middle. The race for The Iron Throne is heating up, the Toilet Bowl is calling two managers' names, and the league bank is getting fat off those FAAB taxes.

That's the Week 4 wrap, NUT League faithful. This is Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan reminding you: in dynasty football, you're only as good as your last Sunday -- and next week, we do it all over again. Until then, keep your rosters tight and your FAAB powder dry. We'll see you next week on THE NUTCAST!

title: Week 3: The Undefeated Three and the Winless Three
synopsis: Week 3 separates the contenders from the pretenders as Prestige Worldwide ascends to the throne while two monster upsets shake the league and The Many-Faced Squad drops 247 points in the biggest blowout of the season.
script:
Ladies and gentlemen, welcome back to THE NUTCAST, the only podcast that matters in the NUT Fantasy Football League! I'm your host, Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, bringing you all the beautiful chaos, all the stunning upsets, and all the dynasty drama from Week 3 of the 2026 season. Strap in, fantasy faithful, because this week we're crowning new kings and watching old favorites fall!

Let's start at the top of the mountain. Prestige Worldwide, piloted by cincy_kid, is your ONLY undefeated team standing at 3-and-0. They climbed to the number one spot in the standings this week by knocking off the formerly undefeated Lickety Splitz Squad, 209 to 187. Now here's the kicker: Prestige Worldwide came in as a half-point underdog. That's right, folks, a HALF-POINT spread, and they covered it by more than 22. George Kittle put up 23.2, Joe Burrow dropped 22.58, and cincy_kid collected a cool ten FAAB bucks from the league bank for beating the spread. Lickety Splitz? They tumbled from first all the way down to fourth in the standings, and even though Will Anderson went absolutely nuclear with 36 points for twillie391, it wasn't enough. De'Von Achane managed just 1.7 points, T.J. Watt gave them 1.75, and suddenly the top team in the league is looking mortal.

But the upset alert didn't stop there. Oh no. The BIGGEST upset of the week came from Points Against Champion, who entered the week as a 26-and-a-half-point underdog against Boom Goes The Dynamite. Let me say that again: 26.5 points. And PAHTNAH's squad walked out with a 192.82 to 189.43 victory in the closest game of the entire week! A margin of just 3.4 points! Sam Darnold led the charge with 29.66 points, and while brandishrewsberry got 28.75 from Greg Rousseau and 25.14 from Bo Nix, it wasn't enough to avoid the upset. Boom Goes The Dynamite drops from third to fifth in the standings, and brandishrewsberry handed ten FAAB dollars right back to the bank. That's the way the cookie crumbles when you can't cover a 26-point spread.

Now let's talk about absolute DOMINATION. The Many-Faced Squad, managed by CamWells16, put up the highest score of Week 3 with a monstrous 247.41 points. They destroyed The OG Champ by 84.4 points in the biggest blowout of the season so far. Bijan Robinson went off for 34.3, Talanoa Hufanga dropped 32.75, and Brock Purdy threw up 31.28. Three players over 30 points each. That's what we call a perfectly balanced attack. The Many-Faced Squad climbed from fourth to second in the standings, improved to 3-and-0, and collected twenty FAAB bucks on TWO separate bets against JeffPeterson20's OG Champ. Meanwhile, The OG Champ falls to 1-and-2 and drops from sixth to eighth. Tyler Nubin put up a goose egg, and the Power Rankings are not kind: The OG Champ slid from fifth down to seventh this week.

Speaking of power moves, White Center Rats climbed from fifth to third in the standings with a 244.26 to 176.82 thrashing of Gus Swayze's Squad. Savro24 got 25.4 from Drake London, 24.8 from Juwan Johnson, and another 24.8 from Tyler Shough. Three players over 24 points, and the Rats now own a perfect 4-and-0 record against AlanCarignan's squad in their all-time head-to-head series. Gus Swayze's Squad? Still winless at 0-and-3, sitting at eleventh in the standings, though the Power Rankings show them climbing from eleventh to ninth, so maybe there's hope on the horizon.

Let's give some love to the league's top individual performers this week. Jahmyr Gibbs absolutely exploded for 37.9 points for Price is wrong BItch, the highest score of any player in Week 3. Will Anderson's 36 points for Lickety Splitz, Bijan Robinson's 34.3 for The Many-Faced Squad, Talanoa Hufanga's 32.75, Brock Purdy's 31.28, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 30.36 for JSN Your Face round out your top six. That JSN performance helped BillsMafia1480 notch his first win of the season, 178.86 to 162.22 over the still-winless Love Hurts. KShrewsberry's squad drops to 0-and-3 and remains anchored at the bottom of both the standings and the Power Rankings.

On the flip side, we had a trio of goose eggs this week. Alex Highsmith for JSN Your Face, Oronde Gadsden for Boom Goes The Dynamite, and Tyler Nubin for The OG Champ all put up zeroes. Jadarian Price managed just 0.7 for Price is wrong BItch in a losing effort against Breece & Desist, who squeaked out a 146.46 to 142.02 victory. Awesomeus covered the 4.5-point spread to get his first win, but Price is wrong BItch lost twenty FAAB bucks on TWO failed bets. That's a rough week at the sportsbook, Smittytribe27.

And finally, your Week 4 Game of the Week is set: The Many-Faced Squad versus Boom Goes The Dynamite. Two teams sitting at 2-and-1 after Week 3, one on a demolition spree and one licking their wounds from an upset loss. Mark your calendars, fantasy faithful.

That's the word from Week 3 of the NUT Fantasy Football League. Three undefeated teams became one, two massive upsets rocked the betting lines, and the race for the Iron Throne is heating up. This is Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan reminding you to set those lineups, trust your gut, and never, EVER, take a half-point spread for granted. Until next week, keep those FAAB budgets ready and those rosters rolling!

title: Week 2: The Undefeated Four and the Winless Four
synopsis: Week 2 draws the battle lines as Lickety Splitz Squad and Prestige Worldwide claim the top two spots while Love Hurts and three others sink to 0-2, plus Devin Lloyd drops 41.5 points and DJ Moore goes negative.
script:
Ladies and gentlemen, football fanatics and fantasy degenerates, THIS is THE NUTCAST, your weekly deep dive into the beautiful chaos of the NUT Fantasy Football League, where The Iron Throne awaits the worthy and the Toilet Bowl haunts the weak. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, and brother, Week 2 just separated the contenders from the pretenders in a hurry.

We've got four teams sitting pretty at 2-0, four teams drowning at 0-2, and the rest fighting for their lives in the middle. Let's break it down.

First, your new number one in the Power Rankings: Lickety Splitz Squad. Twillie391 just hung 241.04 points on JSN Your Face, the highest score of the week by a country mile. Josh Allen out of Buffalo went absolutely nuclear with 40.82 points, slinging it like his life depended on it. Ja'Marr Chase chipped in 23. That's what we call a statement victory, folks. Lickety Splitz moves to 2-0, claims the top spot in both the standings and the Power Rankings with a 94.7 composite score, and they are the hottest team in the league right now.

But don't sleep on Prestige Worldwide. Cincy kid is also 2-0 after absolutely demolishing Love Hurts by 96.4 points, the biggest blowout of Week 2. Jonathan Taylor rumbled for 27.2, Dallas Turner the rookie linebacker out of Minnesota dropped 22, and Prestige Worldwide rolled to 233.74. That 96-point beatdown is the kind of statement that makes opponents check the schedule with dread. Prestige sits at number two in the Power Rankings with an 83.9 score, and they look every bit the part.

Now let's talk about the league's top individual performances, because Week 2 gave us some absolute monsters. Number one on the leaderboard: Devin Lloyd, linebacker for Carolina, rostered by The OG Champ. 41.5 points. Forty-one-and-a-half. Lloyd was an absolute wrecking ball, and that performance helped The OG Champ bounce back from a Week 1 loss by crushing Breece & Desist 232.49 to 161.71. Davante Adams added 37 points in a Rams uniform, Dak Prescott threw for 29.76, and just like that, The OG Champ rockets from twelfth in the standings to sixth. That's how you respond to adversity, folks.

Josh Allen's 40.82 was the second-best performance of the week. Third best? Jaxon Smith-Njigba with 38 points for JSN Your Face, and here's the tragedy: it wasn't even close to enough. JSN Your Face drops to 0-2 despite JSN himself going absolutely bonkers. That's fantasy football, folks. You can get a 38-burger from your namesake receiver and still lose by 81 points.

Rounding out the top performances: Davante Adams at 37, CeeDee Lamb with 31.3 for White Center Rats, and Amon-Ra St. Brown with 30.7 for Price is wrong BItch. The studs were studding in Week 2.

But let's talk about the other side of the coin. DJ Moore out of Buffalo, rostered by The Many-Faced Squad, put up negative 0.1 points. That's not a typo. Negative. You actually lost points by starting DJ Moore this week. Malik Nabers managed just 0.6 for Price is wrong BItch. Colston Loveland, the rookie tight end out of Chicago, gave Love Hurts exactly 0.8 points. Jayden Reed scraped together 0.9 for Breece & Desist. Those are the kinds of performances that haunt your dreams and tank your week.

The closest game of the week came down to Boom Goes The Dynamite edging Gus Swayze's Squad 162.87 to 143.05, a margin of just 19.8 points. Greg Rousseau with 24.5 and Nakobe Dean with 20.75 carried Boom to 2-0, even though they slipped from first to third in the Power Rankings. Meanwhile, Gus Swayze falls to 0-2 despite Travis Kelce dropping 20.6. Sometimes the veteran can't save you.

Let's talk Power Rankings movement because we had some seismic shifts. White Center Rats jumped from fifth to third after demolishing Points Against Champion 210.32 to 144.37. CeeDee Lamb, Jared Goff with nearly 30, and Budda Baker with 22 points powered that victory. The Many-Faced Squad stays undefeated at 2-0 but slips from tenth to sixth in the Power Rankings after beating Price is wrong BItch 192.03 to 148.97. Brock Purdy threw for 28.48, but that DJ Moore goose egg probably cost them some style points.

And then there's the 0-2 club. Love Hurts is dead last at twelve after getting blown out. Gus Swayze's Squad sits at eleven. JSN Your Face at nine and Breece & Desist at ten are both winless, and Breece & Desist took the biggest tumble in the Power Rankings, plummeting from third to ninth after back-to-back losses. When Jayden Reed gives you 0.9 points, you're not winning many matchups.

The Iron Throne is a long way off, folks, but Week 2 showed us who's got the firepower and who's got the holes. Lickety Splitz Squad and Prestige Worldwide look like juggernauts. The OG Champ made a statement. And four teams are staring down the barrel of an 0-2 start wondering where it all went wrong.

That's the week that was in the NUT Fantasy Football League. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan reminding you: in dynasty, every week writes a new chapter, and this one was written in blowouts, breakouts, and bruised egos. Until next week, keep your lineups tight and your FAAB bids tighter. This is THE NUTCAST.

title: Week 1: Boom Goes the Dynamite Explodes
synopsis: The 2026 NUT Fantasy Football League kicks off with fireworks as Boom Goes The Dynamite drops a season-high 252.9 to rocket from dead last to first place, while underdogs bite back and The OG Champ stumbles out of the gate.
script:
Good morning, good afternoon, good evening, wherever you are in NUT Nation -- this is Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, and you are locked in to THE NUTCAST, your weekly audio destination for everything that matters in The NUT Fantasy Football League! We are LIVE for Week 1 of the 2026 season, and folks, if this opening salvo is any indication, we are in for one absolutely electric campaign. Six matchups in the books, twelve teams battling for glory and the Iron Throne, and let me tell you, the first cut is the deepest. Let's crack some shells and see who came to play!

We start at the very top of the leaderboard, where brandishrewsberry and Boom Goes The Dynamite just detonated the scoreboard. Two hundred and fifty-two point nine. Say it with me: two fifty-two point nine! That is not just the week's high score, that is a statement of intent. Boom came into Sunday ranked twelfth in the preseason standings, dead last, but after absolutely torching White Center Rats by 23.7 points, they've launched eleven spots straight to number one. Greg Rousseau on defense put up 32.5, a defensive lineman giving you thirty-two and a half in Week 1, that is house money right there. White Center Rats, by the way, didn't go quietly -- they posted 229.25 behind Derrick Henry's 34.8 and D'Andre Swift's 31.9, and they still took the L. That's dynasty football, folks. Sometimes you bring a cannon to a gunfight and the other guy brought a missile.

Now let's talk about the week's biggest blowout, because twillie391 and the Lickety Splitz Squad put on an absolute clinic. They hung 239.77 on Love Hurts, winning by 87.4 points. Eighty-seven point four! That is not a margin of victory, that is a restraining order. Josh Allen went for 35.66, T.J. Watt put up 34.5, Christian Watson chipped in 29.7, and by the time the dust settled, Love Hurts was limping off the field at 152.35. Lickety Splitz jumped three spots in the standings and now sit at number two. The scary part? They had Kyle Pitts put up a goose egg and still won by nearly ninety. When you can afford a zero from your tight end and still drop 240, you are not a team, you are a problem.

On the flip side, let's pour one out for The OG Champ. JeffPeterson20's squad posted the week's lowest score at 134.6, falling to Price is wrong BItch by 36.3. The OG Champ dropped six spots from sixth to twelfth, and when you're staring at the bottom of the standings in Week 1, you're already eyeing that Toilet Bowl. Jacob Saylors gave you zero. Zero! You can't win in this league when your running back forgets to show up. Price is wrong BItch, meanwhile, rode Jahmyr Gibbs for 31.1 and Amon-Ra St. Brown for 23.7, climbing five spots to sixth. Smittytribe27 is smiling tonight.

Closest game of the week came down to single digits. Prestige Worldwide edged JSN Your Face 223.61 to 214.88, a margin of just 8.7 points. Kenneth Walker put up 32.6 for Prestige, Trevor Lawrence added 26.1, Jonathan Taylor chipped in 23.6, and cincy_kid walked away with the win. BillsMafia1480 had to watch his squad drop seven spots in the standings despite posting 214. That is the cruelest part of fantasy football -- you can score 214 and still lose. You can do everything right and still go home empty.

Now, the upset of the week, the one time the betting line got embarrassed. Breece & Desist came in as a 5.5-point favorite over The Many-Faced Squad, and CamWells16 said not today. The Many-Faced Squad won 215.68 to 193.31, a 22.4-point upset fueled by Bijan Robinson's 27.3 and linebacker Ventrell Miller's 24.25. Awesomeus got a nice game from Bryce Young, 32.44, but when Kyler Murray gives you 0.62, you are cooked. The Many-Faced Squad climbed five spots to fourth, Breece & Desist dropped seven to ninth, and the bookies are licking their wounds.

League-wide standout performances -- Caleb Williams led all scorers with 37.26 for Points Against Champion. The rookie signal-caller is here to play. Josh Allen, Derrick Henry, T.J. Watt, Kenneth Walker, Greg Rousseau, all north of thirty-two points. The league is loaded with talent, and Week 1 showed it.

On the bust side, we had four players put up absolute zeroes: Kyle Pitts, Colston Loveland, Jacob Saylors, and Myles Garrett. Myles Garrett, folks. A defensive end capable of wrecking a game, and he gave Price is wrong BItch a bagel. Somehow they still won. That is the beauty and the brutality of this game.

Power Rankings after Week 1 have Lickety Splitz Squad at number one with a score of 78.1. Prestige Worldwide sits second at 63.1. Breece & Desist dropped to third despite the loss because the algorithm still respects the roster. Points Against Champion, ironically, fell to twelfth in the Power Rankings despite winning their matchup. The numbers never lie, but sometimes they do raise an eyebrow.

Week 1 is in the books. Six winners, six losers, and a whole lot of storylines brewing. The road to the Iron Throne is long, the Toilet Bowl looms for the unlucky, and every week the league bank is watching, waiting to collect those trade and waiver taxes. This is The NUT Fantasy Football League, and this is your Nutcast. I'm Duke 'The Nutcracker' Callahan, reminding you: stay sharp, stay hungry, and never, ever trust a tight end named Kyle. We'll see you next week!
